target_customer: Recruiting and talent acquisition teams at tech and enterprise companies
problem: Recruiters lacked a single system to source, track and measure candidate relationships across email, ATS and social networks.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for recruiting teams
product_category: Talent CRM, sourcing and recruiting platform

founders.name: Steve Bartel
founders.background_notes: YC page: engineering leader at Dropbox who saw recruiting lacked technology. Education not found.

founders.name: Nick Bushak
founders.background_notes: Former Facebook engineer per Domain Name Wire; Greylock says both founders worked at Dropbox and Facebook, so the split is uncertain.

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating with email, ATS systems and LinkedIn data at scale is standard but fiddly engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Becoming the system of record for candidate relationships creates lock in, but ATS vendors and sourcing tools overlap.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: ATS vendors added sourcing features; Gem kept growing and moved into its own ATS.

market_need_then: Greylock said companies spend hundreds of billions of dollars on talent but struggled to track recruiting activity and return; Gem had over 300 customers by mid 2020.

branding.name_origin: Launched as ZenSourcer; renamed Gem in 2019 because customers thought the old name meant sourcing only (Domain Name Wire).
branding.domain_note: Bought gem.com in February 2019; reportedly a seven figure price paid in installments via Escrow.com (a source told Domain Name Wire).

identity.logo: blue logo mark, not further described
identity.voice_and_tone: Positions itself as an AI first all in one recruiting platform

rebrands.why: Old name was restrictive and suggested sourcing only.

branding.community_and_virality: Publishes a recruiting podcast and content, but no evidence of fan or merch culture.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong enterprise reputation and a deliberate, paid for rebrand to an exact match domain, but a generic word and no consumer style community.

pivots.to: Gem talent CRM then full recruiting platform
pivots.why: Brand and product widened beyond sourcing.

outcome_analysis: Gem started as ZenSourcer, rebranded in 2019, and raised 9 million, 37 million and 100 million dollars from Accel, Greylock and ICONIQ, reaching a 1.2 billion dollar valuation in September 2021. It laid off about 100 people in November 2022 after clients cut hiring, then rebuilt around AI and its own ATS. Sources found in 2026 show it independent and operating, which conflicts with the directory status of acquired.
notes: Directory status says Acquired but no acquisition was found; searches in 2026 show Gem independent, so exit.type is none. Possible data error to review. Series A month and Accel as lead come from a search summary; Domain Name Wire confirms 9M in 2019. Total raised was 148M by Series C per company. No competitor sources dated 2017 were found, only current comparison pages. Founder education not found.
